shared_elements: anthropomorphic form (human head in A, human-shaped figure in B)
curved incised bands running across the surface
band of repeated pattern near the upper portion
justification: Both are heavy stone blocks bearing low-relief anthropomorphic carving with curving bands and small disc-like elements, and in each the denser patterning sits toward the upper part of the block. However, A is a rectangular wall slab with a crisply modelled profile head and meticulously repeated rows of curls, while B is a free-standing frontal figure whose shallow, weathered motifs (rings, crescent, girdle-like band) are schematic and sparse, so the manner of carving and the compositional logic differ almost entirely.
